domain.name: dynamic_pricing
domain.one_line: Dynamic pricing of a fixed initial stock over a finite horizon to maximize expected revenue; price-sensitive stochastic (Poisson) demand, no reorder, no backlog.

state_variables.name: period
state_variables.desc: current period t (discretized clock over the finite selling horizon); horizon ends when period == T

state_variables.name: inventory
state_variables.desc: remaining stock n (starts at n0); monotonically non-increasing (no reorder); read by next transition to cap sales

info_fields.name: arrivals
info_fields.desc: raw demand arrivals this period ~ Poisson(lambda(price)*dt), before inventory cap

info_fields.name: lost_demand
info_fields.desc: arrivals that found no stock = arrivals - units_sold (lost, no backlog)

info_fields.name: intensity
info_fields.desc: realized demand intensity lambda(price) = a*exp(-alpha*price) implied by the chosen price

decisions.name: price

type.rationale: the paper's control is a continuous rate; the §4 discrete-price case is a separate variant

bounds.rationale: with a=100, alpha=1 the optimal price p*~1 and run-out prices stay well under ~6; 8 caps the action scale (at p=8 intensity ~= 0.03, effectively the null/shut-off price)

decisions.desc: canonical decision consumed by the _mdp layer: the price charged this period. Agent-facing encodings (price vs intensity) are the gym.action_modes menu.

per_step_components.name: salvage
per_step_components.expr: q * inventory if period == T else 0
per_step_components.desc: terminal component, evaluated at END_OF_PERIOD (period already incremented)

constants.name: a
constants.desc: demand scale: lambda(p) = a*exp(-alpha*p); a=100 is the 'demand high relative to stock' case (Fig 1 bottom)

constants.name: alpha
constants.desc: price sensitivity of the exponential demand family

constants.name: dt
constants.desc: period length = horizon_length/T (unit horizon, T=50); discretization granularity, not a scenario axis

constants.name: q
constants.desc: salvage value per unsold unit at the horizon (WLOG 0 per the paper: positive salvage re-centers price to p-q)

constants.name: allow_backlog
constants.desc: structural: demand arriving with zero stock is lost

constants.name: allow_reorder
constants.desc: structural: no replenishment; inventory is non-increasing

poisson.desc: regular exponential demand family lambda(p)=a*e^{-alpha p}; per-period mean arrivals = lambda(price)*dt where dt = horizon_length/T

action_modes.name: price
action_modes.desc: identity: the agent sets the price directly. Interpretable, but the action scale (upper bound) is a guess and demand is nonlinear in it.

action_modes.name: intensity
action_modes.desc: the paper's native control: agent sets target intensity lambda; transform is p(lambda), the inverse of lambda(p), intensity->0 giving the null (shut-off) price. Naturally bounded box [0, lambda*], lambda* = a/e ~= 36.8 (Prop 1: optimal lambda <= lambda*); revenue is linear in sales — typically easier for PPO.

reward_modes.name: revenue
reward_modes.desc: per-step revenue.total = sales + salvage (sense=maximize, no sign flip)

requires_memory.rationale: fully observed (inventory + time-to-go are the sufficient statistic); no latent source

obs_normalization.rationale: inventory (0–25) and time_to_go (0–50) are stationary, modestly heterogeneous scales; spec §8.3 says normalize

assumptions_log: MODELING CALL (continuous -> discrete): the paper is a continuous-time intensity-control problem; discretized into T=50 equal periods of length dt = horizon_length/T = 0.02. Per-period demand ~ Poisson(lambda(price)*dt). Larger T approaches the continuous point process (mostly 0/1 sales per period); T is a granularity choice.

ACTION ENCODING (price vs intensity): two gym.action_modes (default 'price' = identity/clip; 'intensity' = the paper's native control, a bounded box [0, lambda*] reparametrized to price via p(lambda)). Both drive the same canonical 'price' decision in the _mdp layer; the choice is a gym-layer selection, not a re-formalization.

Demand seed key is derived from realization=period ([stream:1, period, episode_seed, seed_salt]); the primitive is transformed by the CURRENT price via lambda(price), so realized sales are independent of PAST actions (decision-path independence) — current-action dependence is a thinning/time-change of the Poisson primitive.

SCENARIO AXES are the axis-tagged constants: demand (a, alpha; this instance a=100 'demand high relative to stock', the 'ample_stock' instance sets a=20), sizing (n0=25, unit horizon), salvage (q=0 WLOG per the paper).
No backlogging: demand arriving with zero stock is lost (out-of-stock = null price shutting demand off).
EARLY TERMINATION: inventory==0 is absorbing (no reorder), so the episode terminates early; the salvage component is q*inventory = 0 there under any q, so early termination never drops salvage value.
All purchase/production costs are sunk; objective is expected revenue only (sense=maximize).
Out-of-scope §5 extensions omitted from this IR: compound-Poisson demand, time-varying seasonality g(s), holding costs & discounting, initial-stock-as-decision, overbooking/cancellations.
